title: Documentation error in perf_mod
description:
Hi,

I believe there is an error in the `perf_mod` documentation.

## Current Documentation

```r
# Repeated CV (id = repeat, id2 = fold within repeat)
# with a common variance:
statistic ~ model + (model | id2/id)
```

## Suggested change

Since folds (`id2`) are nested within repeats (`id`), the correct formula should be:

```r
# Repeated CV (id = repeat, id2 = fold within repeat)
# with a common variance:
statistic ~ model + (model | id/id2)
```

## Reasoning

The example formula for repeated cross-validation appears to have the nesting operator reversed. Currently, the documented formula produces the wrong model structure as it nests repeats within folds rather than folds within repeats.

In `lme4`/`brms` formula notation, `A/B` means *B is nested within A*, so `id2/id` specifies that `id` (the repeat) is nested within `id2` (the fold), which is the opposite of the actual data structure.

Here's what the `rsample::vfold_cv()` output looks like to confirm that:

```r
library(rsample)
set.seed(1)
vfold_cv(mtcars, v = 3, repeats = 2)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   splits          id      id2  
#>   <list>          <chr>   <chr>
#> 1 <split [21/11]> Repeat1 Fold1
#> 2 <split [21/11]> Repeat1 Fold2
#> 3 <split [22/10]> Repeat1 Fold3
#> 4 <split [21/11]> Repeat2 Fold1
#> 5 <split [21/11]> Repeat2 Fold2
#> 6 <split [22/10]> Repeat2 Fold3
```

Thanks for your help!

title: Consider renaming the `select_best` argument of `perf_mod.workflow_set()`
description:
`perf_mod.workflow_set()` now has a `select_best` argument, added so that workflows fitting the same type of model with the same engine can be collapsed to the best of each group:

```r
perf_mod(wset, metric = "rmse", select_best = TRUE)
```

The method also calls `workflowsets::rank_results(select_best = TRUE)` internally, but for a different purpose: reducing each workflow to its own best tuning parameter candidate. That happens unconditionally and is not affected by the argument.

So the same name means two different reductions a few lines apart:

```r
# R/perf_mod.R:674-690
## Note that `rank_results(select_best = TRUE)` reduces each workflow to its
## own best tuning candidate. That always happens and is separate from the
## `select_best` argument, which reduces the _workflows_ themselves.
ranked <-
  workflowsets::rank_results(object, rank_metric = metric, select_best = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::filter(.metric == metric)

if (select_best) {
  ranked <- dplyr::filter(ranked, wflow_id %in% best_by_engine(object, ranked, metric_dir))
}
```

The comment is there to keep the distinction clear, but a name that can't be confused would be better. Candidates: `best_per_engine`, `one_per_engine`, `collapse_engines`.

This is cheap to change now since nothing depends on the argument yet, and it is not exported anywhere beyond the `perf_mod()` signature. It would become a breaking change after the next release.

Context in `plans/2026-08-27-0843-compare-to-leader.md`, under "Phase 2: choosing which workflows compete".

title: `plot_rope_probs()` seed is always 1 (transposed `sample.int()` arguments)
description:
`plot_rope_probs()` draws the seed for its contrasts with the arguments to `sample.int()` transposed:

```r
# R/posteriors.R:237
model_diffs <- contrast_models(object, l1, l2, seed = sample.int(1, 1000))
```

`sample.int(n, size)` takes the population size first, so `sample.int(1, 1000)` asks for 1000 draws from the set `{1}`. It does not error, because `contrast_models()` only uses `seed[1]`, so the effective seed is always `1`.

Every `autoplot(x, type = "ROPE")` call therefore reuses the same posterior sample rather than drawing a fresh one. That makes the plot reproducible by accident, and it means the `set.seed()` a user sets beforehand has no effect on the contrasts.

The intended call is presumably:

```r
model_diffs <- contrast_models(object, l1, l2, seed = sample.int(10000, 1))
```

which is the form used everywhere else in the package (`tidy.perf_mod()`, `summary.posterior()`, `get_post()`, `contrast_models()` itself).

Worth deciding whether fixing this counts as a user-visible change, since ROPE plots will stop being byte-identical across calls once the seed actually varies.

Found while refactoring the prototype in `plans/2026-08-27-0843-compare-to-leader.md`; noted there under "Out of scope".

title: Feature Request: Crossed random effects for multilevel data
description:
In tidymodels/TMwR#288, I suggested adding the feature of having {tidyposterior} detect multilevel data (e.g., from `rsample::group_vfold_cv()`) and add random effects for the grouping/cluster variable to the model comparison analysis. This would usually be a cross-classified model with random effects (e.g., intercepts) for both resample and group. Accounting for this extra level of dependency in the data is important to properly estimating uncertainty.

I will work on posting some example code below (but am running low on time today).

title: Isn't it a problem that parameters estimation is executed without notification that it is unidentifiable?
description:
Isn't it a problem that parameters estimation is executed without notification that it is unidentifiable?

I was curious about what perf_mod was running and read the [code](https://github.com/tidymodels/tidyposterior/blob/master/R/perf_mod.R) and tidymodels [reference](https://tidyposterior.tidymodels.org/reference/perf_mod.html).

As a result, I understood that rstanarm::stan_glmer was running behind the scenes.
And I understand that stan_glmer is a combination of lme4's glmer and lmer with stan.

I wanted to see how the results would change when I changed the hetero_var without using stan.
When I tried to run the same thing as perf_mod with glmer and lmer
When hetero_var=T, it was stopped by an error code and could not be executed.

However, perf_mod can do it.
We can check for errors after execution, but do we need to stop the user before execution?
I would like to ask if it is necessary to give the user a chance to notice before execution.

Example:

```{r}
library(tidymodels)
library(tidyposterior)

data(two_class_dat, package = "modeldata")

set.seed(100)
folds <- vfold_cv(two_class_dat,v=25)

logistic_reg_glm_spec <-
  logistic_reg() %>%
  set_engine('glm')

mars_earth_spec <-
  mars(prod_degree = 1) %>%
  set_engine('earth') %>%
  set_mode('classification')

rs_ctrl <- control_resamples(save_workflow = TRUE)
logistic_reg_glm_res <- 
  logistic_reg_glm_spec %>% 
  fit_resamples(Class ~ ., resamples = folds, control = rs_ctrl)

mars_earth_res <- 
  mars_earth_spec %>% 
  fit_resamples(Class ~ ., resamples = folds, control = rs_ctrl)

logistic_roc <- 
  collect_metrics(logistic_reg_glm_res, summarize = FALSE) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(.metric == "roc_auc") %>% 
  dplyr::select(id, logistic = .estimate)

mars_roc <- 
  collect_metrics(mars_earth_res, summarize = FALSE) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(.metric == "roc_auc") %>% 
  dplyr::select(id, mars = .estimate)

resamples_df <- full_join(logistic_roc, mars_roc, by = "id")
```

if user perf_mod:

```{r}
perf_mod(hetero_var=T,resamples_df)
perf_mod(hetero_var=F,resamples_df)
```

if I set hetero_var=T, I get an error, but it gets executed.

```
Warning messages:
1: There were 28 divergent transitions after warmup. See
http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#divergent-transitions-after-warmup
to find out why this is a problem and how to eliminate them. 
2: Examine the pairs() plot to diagnose sampling problems
 
3: Bulk Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior means and medians may be unreliable.
Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#bulk-ess 
4: Tail Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior variances and tail quantiles may be unreliable.
Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
http://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#tail-ess 
```

In lme4, it stops before executing.

```{r}
library(lme4)
resamples_df_stan_off <- pivot_longer(resamples_df,
                     cols = c(-dplyr::matches("(^id$)|(^id[0-9])")),
                     names_to = "model",
                     values_to = "statistic")

hetero_F <- statistic ~  model + (1 | id)
hetero_T <- statistic ~  model + (model + 0 | id)

glmer(formula = hetero_T,data=resamples_df_stan_off)
lmer(formula = hetero_T,data=resamples_df_stan_off)
```

```
Error: ... ; the random-effects parameters and the residual variance (or scale parameter) are probably unidentifiable
```

If there is no risk in the implementation of perf_mod, there is no problem.
In that case, I'd like to ask why we don't need to stop as an interest.

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: How to interpret perf_mod and contrast_models results?
description:
I was just wondering if it's possible to interpret the results from the `perf_mod` and `contrast_models` functions using 95% posterior intervals.

Also, I'm not sure if the posterior distribution should (in general) cover the different samples obtained from the `rsample` package. For example, running some code for comparison of different Cox models (for survival analysis), I obtained the plot below. The different concordance indexes for 50 resamples of Monte Carlo cross-validation are shown in blue, and the lines in black corresponds to the posterior distribution after running `perf_mod`. What intrigues me is that the distribution seems too narrow with respect to the spread of the different resamples.

![screen shot 2018-01-02 at 19 24 50](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8128586/34496935-66f18668-eff3-11e7-8660-79dcad692f6c.png)

Sorry for asking this, it's the first time I use the stan R package, and trying to adopt a more Bayesian approach (and mentality) rather than the typical p-values.
